items_missed: No 'How are you today?' and no explicit 'Sound good?' confirmation after describing the process, even though he did explain the agenda (build a profile, ask questions, then talk pricing).
Never asked if packing services were needed or the direct moving-stressors question ('anything you're particularly worried about with this move?').
No 'Pricing is super simple' opener before quoting the hourly rate.
No mention of Meet Your Mover.
Explained variables (stairs, drive time, disassembly, walk distance) well but never used an equivalents reference (e.g., school bus comparison) to make the time estimate concrete.

Save Your Ass was only partially given — hit the core 'prep before move day lowers your bill' point, but skipped the consolidation examples (toys, garden tools, drawers, wall photos), the 'take a carload' tip, and never closed with a 'does that make sense?' check.
Never attempted to lock in the booking on the call itself (let the customer's own 24-hour decision timeline stand without offering to hold the slot now).
Didn't say 'reply with any corrections' for the customer to verify the emailed details.
Never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?'
Didn't give business hours or how to reach the branch.
Never used the customer's name (Laura) once during the call, despite getting it upfront.
top_strength: Walked through the billing mechanics (contract-open clock start, 2.5-hr minimum, 15-min proration, pay-only-for-actual-time) and the No Worries $2,000 coverage vs. the industry-standard 60 cents/lb baseline with real clarity on a genuinely complex 3-stop move, prompting repeated unprompted 'wow' reactions from the customer.
coaching_note: The pricing walkthrough and clock/estimate mechanics were strong, but two of the highest-value moments — the full Save Your Ass prep speech and the Meet Your Mover / On-Time Guarantee differentiators — were skipped or left half-said, and the call never closed with an attempt to hold the booking today or a 'reply with corrections' ask. Tightening the close and finishing the differentiator list would lift this well past mastery without adding call time.
phone_presence_notes: Patient and warm throughout ('no worries,' 'gotcha,' 'not a problem at all'), stayed unbothered through repeated address spelling corrections, and earned genuine enthusiasm from the customer ('Wow' x3, effusive thanks at the close), though he never used her name and had no standout humor moment.
